facts.text: The README describes Gym-like interfaces through ROS for the real Franka Emika Panda arm, for reinforcement-learning prototyping.
The documented deployment has two Ubuntu 18.04 machines: a real-time Linux NUC connected directly to the Franka FCI computer and a second ROS machine connected to the NUC.
The installation assumes ROS Melodic, libfranka 0.5 and franka_ros, with franka_ros built from source on the melodic-devel branch.

Running the Gym environments is documented as launching panda_robot.launch and kinect_azure.launch, then running panda_env_test.py; the test should move the robot along x, y and z in cartesian velocity mode and occasionally reset it to the home configuration.
PandaReacherEnv is the concrete reacher environment class and derives from gym.Env.

PandaReacherEnv.__init__ starts a ROS node named panda_robot_reacher_v0, sets dt to 0.1 s (a 10 Hz rate), and builds PandaClient with the end-effector safety zone [[0.2, 0.7], [-0.3, 0.05], [0.15, 0.4]] and Kinect enabled.
PandaReacherEnv stores hole_goal (0.455, -0.005, 0.25), threshold 0.05, sparse False and _max_episode_steps 50.
PandaReacherEnv.apply_velocity_action copies action[0], action[1] and action[2] into Twist.linear.x, .y and .z and calls PandaClient.set_ee_velocity.
The dense reward is minus the Euclidean distance to hole_goal; the sparse branch returns -(distance >= threshold).
PandaReacherEnv.preprocess_action returns the action unchanged.

PandaReacherEnv.step applies the action, sleeps one rate period, reads the observation, computes the reward and done = distance < threshold, and returns a four-tuple (observation, reward, done, info); it does not test _max_episode_steps.
PandaReacherEnv.reset calls PandaClient.go_home() and returns the observation.
PandaReacherEnv.get_obs concatenates PandaClient.O_P_EE and O_V_EE, the end-effector position and velocity, into one observation.
PandaReacherEnv.close publishes a zero linear velocity through set_ee_velocity.
PandaReacherEnv imports PandaClient as a top-level module (from panda_client import PandaClient), not as a package-relative import.
PandaClient creates actionlib clients for /franka_gripper/homing, /franka_gripper/move and /franka_gripper/grasp.
PandaClient creates an actionlib client for /franka_control/error_recovery.
PandaClient publishes Twist commands on /franka_control/target_velocity with queue size 1 and subscribes to /franka_control/current_target_velocity.
PandaClient subscribes to /franka_state_controller/franka_states with franka_msgs/FrankaState and stores the message in update_state.
PandaClient.set_ee_velocity clips only velocity components that would move the end effector farther outside the configured safety zone, then publishes the Twist on /franka_control/target_velocity.
PandaClient.go_home switches to the position joint trajectory controller when it is not running, moves to a fixed home joint configuration and switches back to the cartesian velocity controller.
PandaClient contains Python 2 print statements, for example print "Waiting for gripper homing server".
PandaClient uses the Python 2 exception syntax except rospy.ServiceException, e:.
The gym package registers panda-robot-reacher-v0 with entry point gym_panda_robot.envs:PandaReacherEnv and panda-robot-reacher-v1 with entry point gym_panda_robot.envs:PandaReacherEnv1.
The envs package imports PandaReacherEnv from panda_reacher_env and PandaReacherEnv1 from gym_panda_robot.envs.panda_reacher_manga; no panda_reacher_manga module exists in the clone.
The top-level package registers panda-robot-v0 with entry point gym_panda_robot.envs:PandaPegInHoleEnv.
PandaPegInHoleEnv imports PandaBaseEnv from panda_base_env; no panda_base_env module exists in the clone.
PandaPegInHoleEnv.step is declared with no action parameter and then refers to an undefined action variable.
The gym package declares only gym as its install dependency.

determinism.notes: the fake accepts the bridge seed and is deterministic without random sampling; its fixed trajectory and placeholders repeat, but this is not the upstream arm or ROS behaviour and was not compared with a live run

fidelity.engine: analytic:pure-Python PandaReacherEnv fake (no ROS, no arm, no physics)
gaps: the fake is a pure-Python analytic stand-in for the old Gym PandaReacherEnv: it does not import gym, rospy, MoveIt, franka_ros, numpy or the clone, never starts a ROS node, and never publishes a Twist or calls a controller, gripper or error-recovery action

the upstream environment is hardware-in-the-loop for a real Franka Emika Panda over ROS (README.md:3,7,49-65; panda_client.py:169-175,320-353); no upstream simulator or mock exists, so the fake is not a recording and no arm trajectory was captured

the action bounds of Box(-1, 1) with three values are placeholders: upstream preprocess_action returns the action unchanged and apply_velocity_action writes action[0..2] to Twist.linear with no value bound, clipping or scale (panda_reacher_env.py:38-43,60-61), so these are not sourced limits

the fake's start position, goal, threshold and velocity gain are placeholders, not calibrated values; the fake integrates one velocity step per tick and models no arm kinematics, controllers, contacts, actuators, gripper, camera or sensor noise

the upstream environment is Python 2 (panda_client.py:105,396) and its envs package imports a missing panda_reacher_manga module (envs/__init__.py:1-2), so the registered old Gym environment cannot be constructed on Python 3 here

no sim or hardware backend is served: only the fake backend is declared; a live ROS deployment would need the Python 2/ROS Melodic stack with libfranka, MoveIt, franka_ros and a real arm, and such a binding would be at least R2 with a human-reviewed independent stop
the fake accepts reset(seed, options) for the bridge while upstream reset() takes no argument and the seed does not change the fake's fixed trajectory

the fake returns the old Gym four-tuple (observation, reward, done, info) and Python lists; upstream returns numpy arrays, a one-element reward and a one-element done array, and the bridge reports done as terminated
the package serves no rendering, snapshot or restore, and the upstream _max_episode_steps=50 is not enforced by the environment's own step

model review r20: the device is a real Franka Panda (an arm, R2) with no hardware-free path, and the only stop-like call, close(), publishes an unacknowledged zero Twist; the package is blocked NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH and this fake contract is not a substitute for that missing path

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: The simulated fake stops advancing: after an e-stop no step, reset or seed is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the placeholder world state stays readable. This is a software latch on an isolated fake, not a robot stop; no hardware or ROS backend is served.
